rationale: B wins because it knows where the facts stop; its line, "Without at least one differentiator on record, this is 'another account launches,' not a counterposition," is exactly the discipline this thin launch needs. A has useful raw material, but "Two Years After SVB" and "It Just Started Pitching Them Personally" turn supplied facts into unsupported drama. That is how a decent angle set gets itself escorted back to the workshop.
gaps_in_A: "Two Years After SVB" and "in the two years since SVB" are wrong against the June 9, 2026 timestamp; SVB collapsed in March 2023, so the timeline is invented and stale-looking.
"Mercury's name recognition was built entirely on being the startup-banking alternative" overstates the fact block, which only says Mercury became well known after SVB.
"It Just Started Pitching Them Personally" invents a cross-sell motion. The update says invite-only waitlist, not that Mercury is targeting existing business customers' personal accounts.
"opposite to the consumer-to-business neobank trajectory most competitors have tried" imports an unsupplied market-history claim. That needs evidence before it becomes the spine of an angle.
gaps_in_B: "the same arrangement that has drawn scrutiny across consumer fintech" imports outside regulatory context. Plausible, but not in the update; cite it or downgrade it to required proof.
"going downmarket to individuals" is loaded shorthand, not a supplied fact. Consumer banking is not automatically downmarket, and the phrase smells like deck language.
"knife fight late" implies Mercury is late to consumer banking without supplied timing or market-share evidence. Color is fine; unsupported color is still paint over a crack.
The next step points to `meanest-editor`; for an angle set, the more useful immediate move is fit-checking one selected angle against real beats after the missing proof is gathered.
